title: Smalls Paradise, John Hammond and Ed Small
summary: Smalls was a black-and-tan place where he met Hammond; a rival's complaint about his Louis-style high notes led Ed Small to tell him to play himself.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: I think Richard Fulbright was playing bass, wasn't he? Yeah, he used to wear them funny hats when he played. Heh-heh...
Yeah. Well, they weren't like the Cotton Club. Blacks and Whites came there. That's where I first met John Hammond.

He used to come there and read the newspaper until the band come on or while the show was on, you know; wait and listen to the band, you know. There used to be a bunch of cats used to come in there, used to wear the high-tail collars, and they always used to like stuff bills in my horn, you know. When they'd come in there, we was good for a yard-and-a-half easy.

It was real nice down there. I was offered a job there with me and Sidney de Paris battling. Because you know, when you got a joint like that, when the boss goes away, there's somebody always that's spying on you. So I guess he must have been a friend of Sidney somehow or another, because he told Ed Small sitting there, "That Little Jazz,

man, he's stinkin' up the joint, hittin' all them high notes, trying to play like Louis Armstrong." When he came back, I was called me into his office, you know. He said, "Play like you play. Forget about them high notes." I just listened.
